problems.note: The explanation 'Three hundreds make 300, and one more 50 makes 350' is muddled. The 300 comes from six jumps of 50, not from three hundreds. Suggested wording: 'Six jumps of 50 make 300, and one more jump of 50 makes 350.' The answer 350 is correct.

Choice d (886) is already printed on the screen as the last number in the sequence, so a child can pick it by matching rather than by counting. Consider a distractor that does not appear in the sequence. The marked answer 786 is correct.

This item counts by 1s, which the skill description includes, so it is in scope. It is also a very easy warm-up, and it is the only item that does not use the 50s, 100s, or 200s focus of the story. The answer 400 is correct.

output.notes: Reviewed the story cards and all 16 items. Every marked answer checks out: 400, 200, 700, 800, 400, 500, 700, 350, 575, 750, 900, 821, 786, 750 and 650. Each tap item has exactly one correct choice, and the VERIFY items were worked out by hand. The story arithmetic is correct: 100/200/300/400, 50/100/150/200, five 200s reach 1000, and 221/421/621/821. No blockers found. The three notes cover one muddled explanation, one distractor that duplicates a number on screen, and one easy item. The number-line items depend on dragging a frog, so a child who cannot read or drag cannot finish them even though the narration is audible. That is an inherent design limit of the activity rather than a content error, so I did not flag it per item.
